summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, bipolar disorder, PTSD, and prior alcohol abuse was admitted for acute on chronic pancreatitis due to two obstructing pancreatic duct stones causing ductal dilation. He presented with severe epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting. Pain was initially managed with IV Dilaudid and transitioned to PCA, then oral medications as symptoms improved. He advanced from sips to a low-fat diet, remained hemodynamically stable, and ambulated throughout the stay. Pre-operative workup including ECG and chest X-ray was completed, and he was discharged home in stable condition to prepare for an upcoming Puestow procedure. Discharge instructions included avoiding NSAIDs, continuing home medications, and follow-up with surgery and primary care.
